key_insight: Magnetism controls atomic ordering in Fe-rich Fe–Si alloys: D0₃ ordering dominates in the fully ordered ferromagnetic state, while B2 ordering is promoted in the elevated-temperature paramagnetic state.
engineering_relevance: Linking magnetic state, lattice expansion, and Si content can guide composition and thermal-processing choices for Fe–Si alloys whose magnetic and mechanical properties depend on atomic order.
method: Calculate magnetically resolved effective cluster interactions using density functional theory.
Model bcc Fe–Si alloys containing up to 20 at% Si using statistical thermodynamics.
Run Monte Carlo simulations to track temperature-dependent ordering and phase behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that Monte Carlo predictions reproduce experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range order characteristics, without providing quantitative agreement metrics.
watch_item: The demonstrated scope is bcc alloys up to 20 at% Si; predictions outside this range require validation.
paper_title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
